alerts.title: EFV CNS toxicity: insomnia and vivid dreams
alerts.message: Guidelines list persistent CNS toxicity such as dizziness, insomnia, and abnormal dreams as a major adverse event of EFV requiring regimen substitution. Patient has been on EFV since February 2024 and now reports poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks. Neuropsychiatric symptoms including bad dreams and insomnia are specifically flagged for EFV in adverse event screening. Symptoms emerging long after initiation suggest persistent toxicity rather than transient early tolerance. No suicidal ideation is documented, which lowers immediate psychiatric risk, but persistence warrants action. Non-drug causes of insomnia were not assessed in the note.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess symptom severity and duration; if persistent CNS toxicity confirmed, substitute EFV per guideline (e.g., switch to alternative agent) and complete aDSM form.

alerts.title: Adverse drug reaction reporting not documented
alerts.message: Guidelines require suspected adverse drug reactions to be documented on the aDSM form and submitted to the National Drug Authority. The clinician's plan for this patient records the insomnia and vivid dreams complaint but lists no orders, no medicine changes, and no adverse event reporting action. Neuropsychiatric symptoms are among the events that should trigger the aDSM screening checklist at every visit. This is a documentation and pharmacovigilance gap rather than a direct clinical harm.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete the aDSM form for the suspected EFV neuropsychiatric adverse event and submit to NDA per national reporting requirements.
